title: Fix batch window shift causing interleaved invoice line timestamp duplication
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers have reported duplicated invoice line timestamps and small negative adjustments on mid-cycle invoices. Investigation points to our hourly usage aggregator sometimes assigning usage events to adjacent hourly buckets when ingestion is delayed or retried. Those mis-bucketed events cause the export reconciler to produce interleaved line items that NetSuite maps to different accounting intervals, which in turn triggers duplicate credits and proration drift.
reproduction_steps: 1) Simulate client traffic with burst + intermittent network errors to produce retried usage events (client-side jitter).
2) Inject delayed ingestion (worker queue delays) so events land several seconds to minutes after original event_time, spanning an hour boundary.
3) Run hourly aggregator with current 'processing_time' bucketing logic and observe events moved into previous/next bucket based on ingestion timestamp.
4) Run export/reconciler to generate Stripe line items and NetSuite CSV; verify duplicated timestamps and out-of-order invoice lines for the same user in adjacent buckets.
root_cause: The hourly usage aggregator currently buckets by processing_time with a loose tolerance window to accommodate late arrivals. Combined with asynchronous retries and rate-limit credit adjustments we sometimes compute two line items for effectively the same usage time range. Our reconciler assumes monotonic, non-overlapping bucket boundaries; when overlaps occur we emit duplicate or interleaved invoice lines and idempotency keys are insufficiently granular (they are derived from bucket_id + customer_id, but bucket_id differs for near-boundary events).
impact_analysis: Affecting ~0.6% of customers with high bursty workloads; typical symptom is duplicate small line items or offset credits on the subsequent invoice. Financial risk includes incorrect revenue recognition for a subset of invoices and increased support tickets. Internal monitoring showed a spike in invoice reconciliation failures and NetSuite import rejections in the last two weeks correlating with a rollout that increased worker parallelism.
proposed_solution: 1) Switch aggregator bucketing to use deterministic event_time bucketing aligned to the customer's billing timezone (falling back to account timezone mapping) rather than processing_time. 2) Enforce an explicit idempotency key computed as sha256(customer_id + event_time_bucket_start + usage_signature) so near-boundary retries map to the same bucket id. 3) Add a sanitize pass in the export reconciler to detect overlapping buckets for a customer within a billing period and merge them deterministically before emitting Stripe/NetSuite lines. 4) Run a targeted backfill for the last 30 days for affected customers and a reconciliation reconciliation job to re-emit corrected exports to NetSuite on a dry-run first. 5) Add unit + integration tests and a synthetic chaos test to simulate ingestion delay and retries.
acceptance_criteria: Aggregator bucketing uses event_time aligned to account billing timezone for all hourly aggregates.
Idempotency keys stable across retries for the same logical usage event (test vectors included).
Export reconciler no longer emits overlapping/duplicate invoice line items in synthetic repros and in staging NetSuite CSVs.
Backfill run completes for a 30-day window with a report summarizing corrected vs unchanged invoices; no net negative revenue beyond current known adjustments.
No increase in NetSuite import rejection rate after rollout; monitoring dashboards updated with alerts on overlap-detection metrics.
